question.text: Yamuna Growth AIF is finalising its audit calendar. Which set of audits does an AIF typically undertake?

answer.text: Only a statutory audit of books of accounts by a CA, once every three years.
Only an internal audit by the Compliance Officer, annually.
Only a PPM audit by a merchant banker, once in the lifetime of the fund.
Annual statutory audit by a qualified auditor, an annual PPM audit performed by a CA or CS, and internal audits — per SEBI (AIF) Regulations and relevant circulars.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7 states: 'Statutory auditors, PPM auditors and Internal auditors are appointed by AIFs as they sign-off on the financial statements, Annual PPM Audit and internal audits, as the case may be. All the books of accounts of the AIF shall be audited annually by a qualified auditor, similarly PPM audit is mandated each year to be performed by a CA or CS.' The Trap: Option A wrongly stretches to 3 years. Option B ignores statutory and PPM audits. Option C wrongly limits PPM audit to a one-time event. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) tests audit-committee governance. XXI-B (PM) has its own independent audit framework under PMS Regs. XIX-C managers must know PPM audit is ANNUAL — a common trap. Manager's Pro-Tip: Schedule the PPM audit in Q1 of each financial year. It drives the annual investor-report template — if your statutory audit and PPM audit are staggered across quarters, your LP-reporting timeline cascades.
